Q2 (a) A compound contains 12% of carbon, 16% of oxygen, 28% of nitrogen, 4% of hydrogen and
40%  calcium  by  weight,  then  what  can  be  the  possible  molecular  formula  of  the
compound?
[2]
 (b) In the production of a drug having a molecular weight of 192, the exit stream from the
reactor flows at a rate of 10.5 L/min. The drug concentration is 41.2% (in water), and the
specific gravity of the solution is 1.024. Calculate the concentration of the drug (in kg/L)
in the exit stream, and the flow rate of the drug in kg mol/min.
[3]

Q3 (a) A solution of ethyl alcohol containing 8.6% alcohol by weight is fed at the rate of 5000
kg/hr  to  a  continuous  fractionating  column  operating  at  atmospheric  pressure.  The
distillate which is the desired product contains 95.4% alcohol by weight and the residue
from the bottom of the column contains 0.1% alcohol by weight. Calculate the mass flow
rates of the distillate and residue in kg/hr
[2]
 (b) A solution of ethyl alcohol containing 8.6% alcohol by weight is fed at the rate of 5000
kg/hr  to  a  continuous  fractionating  column  operating  at  atmospheric  pressure.  The
distillate which is the desired product contains 95.4% alcohol by weight and the residue
from the bottom of the column contains 0.1% alcohol by weight. Calculate the following:
i. the mass flow rates of the distillate and residue in kg/hr, and
ii. the percentage loss of alcohol.
[3]

Q4 (a) It is required to prepare 1250 kg of a solution composed of 12 wt.% ethanol and 88 wt.%
water. Two solutions are  available,  the  first contains  5  wt.%  ethanol, and  the  second
contains 25 wt.% ethanol. How much of each solution are mixed to prepare the desired
solution?
[2]
 (b) A  liquid  containing  47.5%  acetic  acid  and  52.5%  water  is  to  be  separated  by  solvent
extraction using isopropanol. The solvent used is 1.3 kg per kg of feed. The final extract is
found to contain 82% acid on solvent free basis. The residue has 14% acid on solvent free
basis. Find the percentage extraction of acid from the feed.
[3]
